- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.36) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.18) or shows negative drift, especially after recent spikes.
- Avoid sharp upward forecasts after a recent spike; model tends to overreact and overshoot.
- Correct for mean reversion: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For 30-day horizon, reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is weak or shows negative trend over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is rising but price is falling, model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast slightly to avoid overcorrection.
- Don’t assume sentiment directly translates to price; if sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, reduce forecast by 2–5%.
- Forecast should not exceed 15% above 30-day moving average unless sentiment is >0.53 and recent price is trending up.
